data.title: Acuity Files 8K - Entry Into Definitive Agreement >AYI
data.description:
Acuity Inc. (AYI) filed a Form 8K - Entry Into a Definitive Agreement - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on November 20, 2026.

On November 19, 2026, Acuity Inc. ("we," "our," "us," "the Company," or similar references) entered into an Amendment No. 1 (the "Credit Facility Amendment") to that certain Credit Agreement, dated as of May 8, 2026, among the Company, the subsidiary borrowers from time to time party thereto, the various lenders from time to time party thereto, and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., as administrative agent (the "Existing Credit Agreement"; the Existing Credit Agreement, as amended by the Credit Facility Amendment is referred to herein as the "Credit Agreement").

The Credit Facility Amendment, among other things, provides for an unsecured delayed draw term loan facility of up to $400 million (the "Term Loan Facility"). The Credit Agreement permits the proceeds of the Term Loan Facility to be used for general corporate purposes, including to pay a portion of the cash consideration to close the acquisition of Parameter Technologies by Acuity Intelligent Spaces US Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company (the "Acquisition"), at a later date, and to pay fees, premiums, expenses and other transaction costs incurred in connection with the Acquisition. The Term Loan Facility may be drawn in a single borrowing, subject to certain conditions, at any time through the earliest of (i) the date that is six months after the effective date of the Credit Facility Amendment, (ii) the "outside date" (as defined in the definitive acquisition agreement for the Acquisition as in effect on the signing date thereof, giving effect to any extension thereto pursuant to the terms of such definitive acquisition agreement as in effect on the signing date thereof) and (iii) the date of the termination of the Term Loan Facility commitments in accordance with the Credit Agreement. On November 19, 2026, no loans were outstanding under the Term Loan Facility.

The Term Loan Facility will mature on May 8, 2031, which is the maturity date of the revolving loans and commitments under the Existing Credit Agreement. Borrowings under the Term Loan Facility bear interest at a rate equal to an adjusted base rate or Term SOFR, plus, in each case, an applicable margin. The applicable margin is based on, at the Company's option, the Company's leverage ratio or credit rating level. Undrawn commitments under the Term Loan Facility will accrue a facility fee from and including the date that is 91 days after the effective date of the Credit Facility Amendment, which facility fee will be determined, at the Company's option, by the Company's leverage ratio or credit rating level.

The covenants and events of default that apply to the revolving loans and commitments under the Credit Agreement also apply to the Term Loan Facility, and borrowings under the Term Loan Facility are guaranteed by the subsidiaries of the Company that guarantee the revolving loans and commitments.

The foregoing summary of the Credit Facility Amendment, including the transactions contemplated thereby, does not purport to be complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Credit Facility Amendment, filed herewith as Exhibit 10.1 and incorporated herein by reference.

data.title: Proximity Labs Takes Strategic Stake in SVRN with 6.3% Holding
data.description:
Proximity Labs Takes Strategic Stake in SVRN with 6.3% Holding

Proximity Labs disclosed a 6.3% stake in SVRN, Inc., holding 117,647 common shares in a Schedule 13D filed Nov. 20, 2026. It acquired the shares on Oct. 28, 2025, paying nearly $3 million in NEAR tokens before SVRN's 1-for-20 reverse stock split. Its separate Series B preferred shares carry enhanced voting rights, and the group estimates it can exercise up to 9.99% of SVRN's voting power.

Investor Intent

Proximity Labs says it acquired the shares as an investment in SVRN's adoption of a NEAR-focused digital-asset treasury strategy. The group also acquired Series B preferred shares with enhanced voting rights; it says that feature could give its investment the purpose or effect of influencing SVRN's control, rather than serving solely as a passive holding.

The group will keep reviewing its investment and says it may buy or sell SVRN securities, vote its common and preferred shares, and discuss SVRN's business, strategy and governance with management, directors and other shareholders. It has not identified a specific proposal to change SVRN's operations or leadership.

Investor's Background

Proximity Labs is a Cayman Islands company that researches and develops open-source software in the NEAR Protocol ecosystem. Proximity Foundation, a Cayman Islands foundation company focused on blockchain composability and cross-chain projects, is its sole member and director. Kendall Cole and Marc Piano manage the foundation as its two directors and may share voting and investment control over Proximity Labs' SVRN holdings.

data.title: Nasdaq plunges 5% a day after Anthropic debut, but investors still believe in AI
data.description:
Tech stocks slumped on Friday to a 10% weekly decline in the Nasdaq composite , the biggest in two years, matching the pullback in response to the Liberation Day tariff announcements in spring 2025.

Nvidia tumbled 14% on Friday and 23% for the week after Reuters reported the Securities and Exchange Commission was probing its accounting. Anthropic dropped 9% after earlier falling as much as 14% following its blockbuster IPO, and the semiconductor index of AI favorites fell 11% in a broad retreat from risk.

For the day, the Nasdaq dropped 5.3%, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX fell 3.7% and Wall Street's fear gauge, the VIX volatility index, soared 33% to 37. The yield on the 10-year US Treasury note fell 12 basis points to 4.93%.

Even so, investors largely said they continued to believe in the AI trade, which took markets to record highs as recently as last month.

COMMENTS:

MICHAEL MONAGHAN, PORTFOLIO MANAGER AND PARTNER AT FOUNDER ETFS, DALLAS, TEXAS:

"In the short run, sentiment drives prices. In the long run, fundamentals do. Right now the market is selling first and asking questions later. In our view, the fundamentals remain strong, and we expect prices to reflect them over time."

GENE GOLDMAN, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER AT CETERA, EL SEGUNDO, CA:

"This week’s chip earnings were an earnings test, and they passed it. Yesterday’s AI IPO is a valuation test, and with the 10-year around 5% and the Fed still hiking, investors are asking how much of the AI story is already priced in."

RICHARD SAPERSTEIN, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER, TREASURY PARTNERS, NEW YORK:

"The stock market is going through an AI repricing, reflecting an environment of slowing data center buildouts, reduced funding sources for AI-related projects and a slower trajectory of technology-related earnings growth. This has been exacerbated by the Nvidia crisis and the Democratic midterm win, which were a one-two punch for the AI story.

"Investors are broadly reducing exposure to technology and AI-related equities in favor of non-technology sectors, such as health care, energy and utilities.

"Within technology, we still like the hyperscalers, which can benefit from any slowing data center buildouts since they already own many of them, and cybersecurity, as the recent wave of cyber outages increases demand for their products.

"Investors should maintain long-term allocations to large cap technology stocks, as AI adoption will continue to accelerate and drive economic growth and productivity. A slowdown in AI spending will extend the cycle over a longer time period. In the near term, hyperscaler capital expenditures may begin to slow, giving rise to free cash flow."

MARK HACKETT, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST FROM NATIONWIDE FINANCIAL, DOWNINGTOWN, PENNSYLVANIA:

"The current environment is reminiscent of the market action surrounding Liberation Day and the breakout of the conflict with Iran. Those resolved quickly as the reality did not match the fear, with retail investors aggressively buying the dip and indexes returning to record highs within months.

"After months of rotational price action, the recent de-grossing feels as though it has arrived gradually, then suddenly. A capitulatory washout could ultimately prove constructive. If this evolves into a true flush, it may serve as the reset needed to improve positioning, sentiment, and the odds of a more sustainable rally into year-end. The fundamental backdrop remains strong, and sentiment and positioning are supportive from a contrarian standpoint, but picking bottoms is difficult when the market is so emotional."

TIM GHRISKEY, SENIOR PORTFOLIO STRATEGIST AT INGALLS & SNYDER IN NEW YORK:

"Interest rates are going up and we have signs of consumer inflation. The Fed is likely to raise rates at the December meeting and possibly the January meeting as well. Financial markets hate higher interest rates. It's medicine that's often necessary to break down inflation. A lot of the inflation is energy related, oil related, but, that finds its way into various other goods and services.

"In general, you know, we have an increasing interest rate environment. We have for a while, and the market sort of has been ignoring it somewhat but it's out there. Since mid-October when the slide began to happen there's been more awareness of it. Fed speakers have been talking about it more. We've had a lot of Fed speak, especially this week. That's the overriding issue.

"The other issue technology in general and AI. Some of that is valuation related and some is the disruption at Nvdia. It was the largest company in the US market and now it’s not. It's had this drama and currently a lack of leadership. It's clear to us that the CFO, who's the interim CEO, as well as keeping her CFO job and everything else, is probably a bit overwhelmed by all of this."

PHILIP PALUMBO, CEO AND CIO, PALUMBO WEALTH MANAGEMENT, NEW YORK:

"In the short term, markets move based on sentiment, emotion, headlines, and investors’ opinions about what may happen next. Fear and uncertainty can drive prices lower, sometimes very quickly.

"But over time, what matters most is the underlying value of the businesses we own. Their earnings, cash flow, competitive advantages, and ability to grow ultimately determine their long-term value. That is where our attention remains focused."

JIM AWAD, SENIOR MANAGING DIRECTOR AT CLEARSTEAD ADVISORS LLC IN NEW YORK:

"You have a growth fear in terms of the economy because of the wealth destruction in the stock market, because of fears of moderation in AI spending, and fears that Nvidia problems will spread beyond Nvidia. So you haven't yet seen a significant deceleration in profit estimates for next year. But that would naturally follow if this turbulence continues. But my expectation is that the turbulence will pass, stock prices will recover, and interest rates on balance will be higher over coming months."

LAWRENCE GILLUM, CHIEF FIXED INCOME STRATEGIST AT LPL FINANCIAL, FORT MILL, SOUTH CAROLINA:

"Right now, we think that this is just kind of more technical in nature and not necessarily something that is broadly concerning. We still think that the AI trade has legs. So we think that this is kind of not a bubble bursting, if you will. This is just kind of just some growing concerns, and adding to those concerns is just this time of the year.

"There's a lot of investors out there who are trying to kind of keep their gains for the year. So they're kind of selling now and asking questions later. So that's not really helping. So those are all things that are potentially pushing downward pressure on the equity markets. But that's been a good thing for the Treasury market in terms of that safe haven status.

"The Fed minutes came out this week and suggested that the Fed is pretty unified about higher interest rates. So we still think that that's likely going to happen. One of the things that's helping with the growth and inflation story, at least from the fixed income markets perspective, is if you think about just how much of a tailwind to economic growth the AI capex has been.

"If that slows a little bit, then potentially, economic growth slows a little bit, inflation comes down a little bit, and maybe the Fed doesn't have to hike as aggressively as what markets are pricing in. And in that scenario, that would help Treasury markets as well... It's a little bit more concerning perhaps on the economic growth side, but we don't think recession is in the cards anytime soon."

data.title: Energy Vault Holdings, Inc. Announces New Hire Awards Under NYSE Listing Rule 303A.08

Energy Vault Holdings, Inc. (“Energy Vault”) (), a global energy storage company today announced that, effective on November 4, 2026, the Compensation Committee of Energy Vault’s Board of Directors granted to 22 new employees restricted stock unit awards covering an aggregate 1,230,250 shares of its common stock under the Energy Vault Holdings, Inc. 2022 Employment Inducement Award Plan (as amended and/or restated, the “Plan”). Energy Vault® is an integrated power infrastructure platform that builds, owns and operates flexible, reliable energy systems to accelerate time-to-power for utilities, independent power producers, industrial customers and the AI and data center market. At the core of its platform is a technology-agnostic, software-enabled architecture that is designed to accelerate project delivery, optimize performance and drive faster time-to-revenue. Energy Vault’s integrated solutions combine energy storage, generation and advanced energy management to deliver scalable infrastructure tailored to customer needs. Its portfolio spans short-, long- and multi-day duration storage, designed to enable reliability, flexibility and cost efficiency across applications. For utilities and grid operators, Energy Vault provides firm, flexible capacity that ​enhances grid stability and helps to ensure reliable power delivery. For industrial and data center customers, the platform enables resilient, cost-efficient power supply to support critical operations. Through its Build, Own & Operate model, Energy Vault generates long-term, recurring revenues while delivering project execution excellence across development, delivery and operations. By combining innovation with disciplined execution, Energy Vault is redefining how power infrastructure is developed and deployed – delivering reliability, flexibility and scale in a rapidly evolving global energy market. data.title: Dynagas LNG Partners LP Reports Results for the Three and Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026
data.description:
ATHENS, Greece, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Dynagas LNG Partners LP (the “Partnership”), an owner of liquefied natural gas (“LNG”) carriers, today announced its results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Nine Months Highlights:

  • Net Income and Earnings per common unit (basic and diluted) of $51.9 million and $1.29, respectively;
  • Adjusted Net Income(1) of $46.6 million and Adjusted Earnings per common unit(1) (basic and diluted) of $1.14;
  • Adjusted EBITDA(1) of $82.0 million; and
  • 97.1% fleet utilization(2).

Quarter Highlights:

  • Net Income and Earnings per common unit (basic and diluted) of $18.6 million and $0.46, respectively;
  • Adjusted Net Income(1) of $18.4 million and Adjusted Earnings per common unit(1) (basic and diluted) of $0.46;
  • Adjusted EBITDA(1) of $30.1 million;
  • 100% fleet utilization(2);
  • The Arctic Aurora was delivered under its new time charter party agreement with Rio Grande LNG, LLC (“Rio Grande”) on September 15, 2026;
  • Declared and paid a cash distribution of $0.5625 per unit on the Partnership’s Series A Preferred Units (NYSE: DLNG PR A) for the period from May 12, 2026 to August 11, 2026; and
  • Declared a quarterly cash distribution of $0.050 per common unit for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, which was paid on August 28, 2026, to all common unitholders of record as of August 24, 2026.

(1) Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted Earnings per common unit and Adjusted EBITDA are not recognized measures under U.S. GAAP. Please refer to Appendix B of this press release for the definitions and reconciliation of these measures to the most directly comparable financial measures calculated and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP and other related information.

(2) Please refer to Appendix B for additional information on how the Partnership calculates fleet utilization.

Recent Events:

  • On November 12, 2026, the Partnership completed the partial redemption of its Series A Preferred Units, redeeming 2,000,000 of its 3,000,000 outstanding Series A Preferred Units, which was announced on October 9, 2026, at a redemption price of $25.00 per unit, or $50.0 million in aggregate. Following the partial redemption, 1,000,000 Series A Preferred Units remain outstanding;
  • Declared a quarterly cash distribution of $0.5625 per unit on the Partnership’s Series A Preferred Units for the period from August 12, 2026 to November 11, 2026, which was paid on November 12, 2026 to all Series A Preferred unitholders of record as of November 4, 2026; and
  • Declared a quarterly cash distribution of $0.050 per common unit for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, which is payable on November 20, 2026 to all common unitholders of record as of November 13, 2026.
  • For an update on the current status and potential impact on us of applicable sanctions, please see “Russian Sanctions Developments” below.

CEO Commentary:

We are pleased to report a strong third quarter. Adjusted EBITDA rose 9.2% year on year to $30.1 million and Adjusted Net Income increased 29.3% to $18.4 million, as the fleet operated at 100% utilization and our fleet-wide Time Charter Equivalent (TCE) rate reached $75,027 per day, up 11.8% on the third quarter of 2025 and 7.0% on the previous quarter. This TCE comfortably exceeded our cash breakeven for the quarter of approximately $47,100 per day. The quarter benefited from the first full three months of the Clean Energy’s charter with Rio Grande and from a further 30.8% year-on-year reduction in net interest and finance costs.

Commercially, the Arctic Aurora commenced its new time charter with Rio Grande on September 15, 2026, securing its employment until at least August 2033. With two of our six vessels now chartered to Rio Grande, alongside our long-standing charters with SEFE and Yamal Trade, our fleet is fully contracted for the remainder of 2026 and for 2027, and 65% contracted for 2028. As of the date of this release, our estimated contracted revenue backlog stands at $700 million, with an average remaining contract term of 4.2 years.

Our balance sheet continued to strengthen. During the first nine months of 2026 we repaid $33.1 million of debt, reducing our outstanding financial liabilities to $245.6 million, while our cash increased to $79.9 million at September 30, 2026 from $41.0 million at the end of 2025. At the same time, we continued to return capital to our unitholders, maintaining our quarterly distribution of $0.050 per common unit and paying the full distributions on our Series A Preferred Units. After the quarter end, on November 12, 2026, we redeemed 2,000,000 of our Series A Preferred Units, two-thirds of the class, for $50.0 million, which reduces our annual preferred distributions by $4.5 million.

Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 Financial Results

Net Income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $18.6 million as compared to $18.7 million for the corresponding period in 2025, which represents a decrease of $0.1 million, or 0.6%. The decrease in Net Income was mainly attributable to the Other income which was recognized in the third quarter of 2025, and the increase in Voyage expenses and Vessel operating expenses. The above decrease was substantially offset by (a) the increase in Voyage revenues and (b) the decrease in Net interest and finance costs as explained below.

Adjusted Net Income (a non-GAAP financial measure) for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $18.4 million, compared to $14.2 million for the corresponding period in 2025, which represents a net increase of $4.2 million, or 29.3%. This increase was mainly attributable to (a) the increase in cash Voyage revenues as explained below, and (b) the decrease in Net interest and finance costs which was partially offset by the increase in Vessel operating expenses.

Voyage revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $44.0 million, compared to $38.9 million for the corresponding period in 2025, which represents a net increase of $5.1 million, or 13.1%. This increase was mainly attributable to: (a) the higher time charter rate earned by the Clean Energy under its time charter with Rio Grande, which commenced on April 30, 2026, (b) the increase in variable hire revenues earned under the OPEX pass-through time charters of the Yenisei River and the Lena River, (c) the increase in Revenue earning days, as the fleet operated at full utilization during the quarter compared to the corresponding period of 2025, (d) the non-cash effect of the amortization of deferred revenue, (e) a ballast bonus of $0.9 million due to the Partnership upon the redelivery of the Arctic Aurora by Equinor and (f) the increase of the value of the EU ETS emissions allowances (“EUAs”) due to the Partnership by the charterers of its vessels (the corresponding value of the EUAs, which the Partnership is obliged to surrender to the EU authorities, is included within Voyage expenses, therefore the net effect of the EUAs to the Operating Income and Net income is zero). The above increase was partially offset by the lower time charter rates earned by the Arctic Aurora under its charter with Equinor until September 15, 2026 and under its new time charter thereafter, compared to the corresponding period in 2025.

The Partnership reported average daily hire gross of commissions(3) of approximately $74,820 per day per vessel for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $69,960 per day per vessel for the corresponding period in 2025. The Partnership’s vessels operated at 100% and 99.1% fleet utilization during the three-month periods ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Vessel operating expenses were $8.9 million, which corresponds to a daily rate per vessel of $16,121 for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, compared to $8.1 million, or a daily rate per vessel of $14,594 in the corresponding period in 2025. This increase was mainly attributable to increased crew costs and higher repairs and maintenance costs. As mentioned above, a substantial part of the increase in Vessel operating expenses is counter-balanced by the corresponding increase in variable hire revenues earned on the Partnership’s vessels operating under OPEX pass-through time charters.

Adjusted EBITDA (a non-GAAP financial measure) for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $30.1 million, compared to $27.6 million for the corresponding period in 2025. The increase of $2.5 million, or 9.2%, was mainly attributable to the above-mentioned increase in cash Voyage revenues, which was partially offset by the increase in Vessel operating expenses.

Net interest and finance costs were $3.7 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $5.3 million in the corresponding period in 2025, which represents a decrease of $1.6 million, or 30.8%, mainly due to (i) the decrease in the interest on our Sale and Leaseback Agreements, as a result of the reduction in interest-bearing debt and the decrease in the weighted average interest rate from 6.50% in the three months ended September 30, 2025 to 5.94% in the three months ended September 30, 2026, (ii) the interest expense of $0.4 million on the Series B Preferred Units for the period from July 1, 2025 to their redemption date on July 25, 2025, which was included in the corresponding period of 2025, and (iii) the increase in interest income.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Partnership reported both basic and diluted Earnings per common unit and Adjusted Earnings per common unit (a non-GAAP financial measure), of $0.46, after taking into account the distributions relating to the Series A Preferred Units on the Partnership’s Net Income/Adjusted Net Income. Earnings per common unit and Adjusted Earnings per common unit, basic and diluted, were calculated on the basis of a weighted average number of 36,382,011 common units outstanding during the period and in the case of Adjusted Earnings per common unit, after reflecting the impact of certain adjustments presented in Appendix B of this press release.

Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted EBITDA, and Adjusted Earnings per common unit are not recognized measures under U.S. GAAP. Please refer to Appendix B of this press release for the definitions and reconciliation of these measures to the most directly comparable financial measures calculated and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

Amounts relating to variations in period-on-period comparisons shown in this section are derived from the condensed financial statements presented in Appendix A hereto.

(3) Average daily hire gross of commissions is a non-GAAP financial measure and represents voyage revenue excluding the non-cash time charter deferred revenue amortization, non-hire income such as ballast bonuses, as well as the revenues attributable to the value of the EUAs to be provided to the Partnership pursuant to the terms of its agreements with the charterers, divided by the Available Days in the Partnership’s fleet as described in Appendix B.

Liquidity/ Financing/ Cash Flow Coverage

During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Partnership generated net cash from operating activities of $35.0 million, compared to $26.5 million in the corresponding period in 2025, which represents an increase of $8.5 million, or 32.0%, mainly as a result of working capital changes.

As of September 30, 2026, the Partnership reported total cash of $79.9 million. The Partnership’s outstanding financial liabilities as of September 30, 2026, under the Sale and Leaseback Agreements between the vessel owning companies of the Clean Energy, the OB River, the Amur River and the Arctic Aurora and China Development Bank Financial Leasing Co. Russian Sanctions Developments

Due to the ongoing Russian war with Ukraine, the United Kingdom (the “U.K.”), the European Union (“E.U.”), the United States (“U.S.”) and other countries and organizations have publicly announced and enacted extensive sanctions against Russia to impose severe economic pressure on the Russian economy and government.

Two of our vessels, the Yenisei River and Lena River (the “Vessels”), are employed by Yamal Trade Pte. Ltd. (the “Charterer”) under long-term time charters that extend to 2033 and 2034, respectively (the “Yamal Charters”). Since the commencement of the Yamal Charters, the Vessels have been engaged in the transportation of LNG produced in Russia for discharge at destinations worldwide (the “Yamal LNG Transportation”) in compliance with applicable sanctions regulations.

U.K. Sanctions

On May 20, 2026, the Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/543) came into force in the U.K., amending the Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019. The amendments introduced new Regulations 46Z29B to 46Z29D, which prohibit U.K. persons from directly or indirectly supplying or delivering Russian-origin LNG by ship, and from providing or facilitating related services. The ban covers shipments from Russia to third countries as well as between third countries and is subject to limited exceptions and licensing arrangements. For supply contracts with a duration exceeding one year that were executed before June 17, 2025 and have not since been amended, other than by amendments falling within specified categories, there is a transitional exception that covers relevant activities carried out before January 1, 2027.

As a result, following expiry of the applicable transitional exception, U.K.-based providers of financial services, including the insurers that currently provide protection and indemnity (“P&I”) and hull and machinery (“H&M”) insurance for the Vessels, will be prohibited from providing cover for voyages carrying Russian-origin LNG, unless an applicable exception or licence permits such cover. The U.K. prohibition does not extend to technical services, including classification.

As of the date of this press release, discussions with alternative insurance providers are ongoing; however, we have not secured replacement P&I or H&M insurance for the Vessels and there can be no assurance that such insurance will be in place by January 1, 2027, or that it will be available on comparable terms, or at all. If such insurance is not in place, this could give rise to disputes under the Yamal Charters, including disputes concerning the respective rights and obligations of the Charterer and us under the Yamal Charters. Any such dispute could result in claims that the Vessels are off-hire, additional costs, loss of revenue, litigation or early termination of the Yamal Charters, among other things. Any of these developments could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows and our ability to make distributions to our unitholders and could result in an event of default under our debt agreements, among other things.

E.U. Sanctions

On October 23, 2025, the E.U. adopted the 19th package of sanctions (the “19th Package”), which prohibits the purchase, import or transfer, directly or indirectly, by E.U. persons and non-E.U. persons with an E.U.-nexus, of LNG that originates in Russia or is exported from Russia (the “LNG Prohibition”). The LNG Prohibition applies from January 1, 2027 with respect to supply contracts with a duration exceeding one year (“Long Term Contracts”) that were executed before June 17, 2025 and that have not since been amended, other than by amendments falling within specified categories.

On July 23, 2026, the E.U. amended the 19th Package with the adoption of the 21st package of sanctions (the “21st Package”). The 21st Package introduced an exemption to the LNG Prohibition, initially until July 25, 2027, and thereafter for successive periods of one year, unless the Council of the E.U. (the “E.U. Council”), following an annual review, decides otherwise. The exemption applies to transfers of LNG destined for third countries and, where relevant, purchases associated with those transfers, pursuant to Long Term Contracts that were executed before February 24, 2022 and that have not since been amended, other than by amendments falling within specified categories, provided that the volume of LNG transferred each year under the exemption does not exceed the volume of LNG transferred in 2025 under its qualifying existing Long Term Contract, irrespective of destination (the “Legacy Contract Derogation”).

We, and our sanctions counsel, believe that the transportation of LNG under the Yamal Charters to destinations outside the E.U. currently falls within the Legacy Contract Derogation and, accordingly, is outside the scope of the LNG Prohibition. However, there can be no absolute guaranteed assurance that our interpretation of the Legacy Contract Derogation is correct, or that regulatory authorities or our counterparties will agree with our interpretation. Furthermore, there can be no absolute guaranteed assurance that the transportation of LNG under the Yamal Charters will continue to meet the requirements of the Legacy Contract Derogation, including with respect to the yearly volume limitation, or that the E.U. Council will not decide, following an annual review, to shorten or terminate the Legacy Contract Derogation, or that sanctions regulations will not be further implemented, amended, or expanded to restrict the transportation of Russian-origin LNG.

These risks are outside of our control, and if one or more of these events were to occur, the Vessels would be restricted from transporting LNG originating in or exported from Russia, which would affect the Charterer’s ability to continue employing the Vessels in the Yamal LNG Transportation. Notwithstanding the foregoing, we believe the Yamal Charters would remain enforceable, although their sanctions-specific provisions may suspend performance and, at a later stage, payment of charter hire. The Charterer may not agree with our interpretation, which could result in disputes, Charterer non-performance, litigation or early termination of the Yamal Charters, among other things. Any of these developments would have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition, cash flows and our ability to make distributions to our unitholders and could result in an event of default under our debt agreements, among other things.

U.S. Sanctions

On September 18, 2026, the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (the “Graham Act”) was enacted in the U.S. Among other things, the Graham Act authorizes the President to impose sanctions on foreign vessels that the President determines knowingly transport LNG or certain other energy products originating in Russia, and on persons that provide services to such vessels. On October 16, 2026, the President issued Executive Order 14436, which waived the application of the sanctions, restrictions and duties provided for in the Graham Act. The waiver has no fixed expiration date, and it may be revoked or modified at any time. No sanctions have been imposed on us or the Vessels under the Graham Act. However, there can be no assurance that the waiver will remain in effect, or that sanctions will not be imposed under the Graham Act on us, the Vessels, the Charterer or our service providers, which could restrict or prevent the employment of the Vessels under the Yamal Charters and affect our access to insurance, financing and other services.

Our fleet consists of only six LNG carriers and we derive all our revenues from a limited number of charterers. For the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, the Charterer accounted for approximately 34% of our total revenues, and the charter revenue expected to be generated by the Yamal Charters constituted approximately 56% of our estimated contract backlog. data.title: Stellantis recalls over 82,000 Ram trucks over ABS software risk
data.description:
Stellantis recalled 82,843 Chrysler Ram pickup trucks due to an anti-lock brake, ABS, software issue that increases crash risk, the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Thursday.

The ABS module software could potentially misread inputs from the brake pedal and pedal sensor.

  • The recall is for certain Ram 1500 Classic pickup trucks, manufactured between 2022 and 2024, and 669 of Chrysler's Mopar ABS control modules

  • NHSA cited the recall was due to the risk of improper brake light illumination, unintentional vehicle movement, or a loss of driver-assist features, such as electronic stability control, AutoPark and forward collision warning

  • US-listed shares of the Fiat and Citroën owner, which were down nearly 70% so far this year, fell about 5% on Friday

  • The regulator said Chrysler dealers will update the ABS module software free of charge

  • The company, along with Ford, Honda and Volkswagen, sued New Jersey earlier in the day to block a state law governing how much automakers must pay dealers for warranty and recall repairs

Valvoline continues to build and acquire new stores to extend its growth momentum asa larger percentage of its store network matures, but this aggressive store expansion strategy is capital intensive and limits free cash flow generation, JPM analyst Jeffrey Zekauskas said.

A decrease in oil prices from an opening of the Strait of Hormuz would provide a meaningfulbenefit to margins over time by lowering raw material costs, and Zekauskas said such a possibility is part of a core long-term investment thesis for the company; conversely, higher oil prices would most likely pressure volumes and margins.

data.title: Apollo, Goldman lead $44 billion SpaceX GPU debt financing
data.description:
Apollo and Goldman Sachs have priced a roughly $44 billion debt package to finance SpaceX's acquisition of Nvidia's GPU chips and related equipment, marking what the firms said is the largest AI-related chip financing ever arranged.

Investor demand exceeded supply, allowing the transaction to be upsized. The proceeds are expected to help bankroll SpaceX's deployment of Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin chips as it expands its terrestrial AI computing footprint.

The $25.17 billion of senior secured A3 notes maturing in April 2033 priced at a yield of 8.259%, according to a source familiar with the sale.

About $4.4 billion of senior secured A2 notes maturing in April 2031 were sold at 7.66%, the source said, while $2.564 billion of class B subordinated secured April 2033 notes were sold at 8.36%.

The deal underscores the large capital requirements of the AI boom as technology companies race to secure advanced processors and build out computing infrastructure needed to support AI development.

Lease schedules are expected to start when the GPUs and related equipment are delivered in the first half of 2027

BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management and accounts advised by KKR provided anchor commitments for the transaction, the statement said.

SpaceX said last month that an affiliate of Apollo Global Management would buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the company in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion.

data.title: Wall St ends sharply lower on AI selloff, S&P 500, Dow in correction
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic down sharply a day after debut
  • Intuit down after it cuts revenue forecast, agrees to sell unit
  • Caterpillar falls on demand concerns for AI-related energy generation equipment
  • Cryptocurrency firms slide on bitcoin weakness

By Stephen Culp and Utkarsh Hathi

US stocks extended their rout on Friday, and the S&P 500 and the Dow both confirmed corrections after Anthropic's momentous debut fell flat, exacerbating worries over the AI trade that has driven this year's stock market rally.

All three major US equity indexes ended sharply lower. The Dow and the S&P 500 are now more than 10% below their record closing highs, confirming both indexes have entered correction.

The bellwether S&P 500 notched its seventh consecutive drop, its longest losing streak since February 2020.

All three indexes logged their largest weekly percentage losses since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced his market-rattling "liberation day" tariff package.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq dipped into negative territory for the year.

"This is clearly a challenging day for capital markets, and as we head into a Friday close, appears to be accelerating to a certain degree," Bill Northey, senior investment director at US Bank Wealth Management in Billings, Montana. "But as we step back and evaluate fundamentals and sentiment, sentiment is clearly winning the day today."

"Sentiment is always the more powerful force in the immediate space, whereas fundamentals tend to win out over time," Northey added, referring to economic strength and solid corporate earnings, among other things.

Anthropic's supersized debut as a publicly held company, which was intended to raise as much as $2 trillion in market cap, failed to catch fire on Thursday, closing 17.1% above its $83 offer price as enthusiasm for the stock faded throughout the session.

In its second day as a publicly held company, Anthropic's shares posted a steep loss.

The Anthropic IPO, combined with Nvidia's quarterly earnings report, failed to dispel fears over risks associated with artificial intelligence and the massive expenditures on the nascent technology.

"Nvidia reported what might have been one of the greatest quarters in corporate earnings history; they did everything right," said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services in Hammond, Indiana. "A lot of people, myself included, were looking to the Anthropic debut to some extent as a clearing event, and it wasn't."

The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index , which has powered much of the broader stock market's gains in recent months, was up as much as 106.6% in mid-June. That luster has faded.

Hyperscalers Amazon and Meta tumbled.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius also posted steep losses on the day.

The tech selloff has prompted a rotation into more defensive sectors such as staples and healthcare .

According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 257.38 points, or 3.59%, to end at 6,918.45 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 1,225.05 points, or 5.13%, to 22,654.15. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 908.88 points, or 1.85%, to 48,188.18.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said the central bank's policy rate is not high enough to deal with inflation levels.

Markets are pricing a near-certain likelihood of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike at the Fed's next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

A report from the University of Michigan survey showed post-election consumer sentiment rose to 7.3%.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Among other movers, Intuit shares fell after the company cut its annual revenue growth forecast and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times as much.

UnitedHealth rose after TD Cowen upgraded its shares to a "buy" from a "hold" rating.

The AI selloff also sent Caterpillar shares lower on worries over weakening demand for its power-generating and backup power equipment.

Bitcoin dropped below the $60,000 level, weighing on cryptocurrency firms including Coinbase , Strategy and Robinhood .
